title: One-shot Primitives are structurally sealed after use rather than left available for re-invocation
content:
Four of Spark's Primitives repeat the same closing statement in both their In Progress Invocations directories and their Operational Process Definitions: because the Primitive "is deployed solely for the one-time creation / transformation of the Agent" (or "the one-time deployment of the Agent's token"), "no further Instances of the Primitive can be Invoked" and "no further operational process is needed post-deployment" — see A.6.1.1.1.2.1.1.1.4, A.6.1.1.1.2.1.2.1.4, A.6.1.1.1.2.1.3.4 and A.6.1.1.1.2.1.4.4.

This distinguishes **Genesis Primitives** from **Operational Primitives**. The Genesis set describes acts that constitute an entity — creating the Agent, typing it as a Prime Agent, deploying its token. Those acts are not repeatable without producing a different entity, so the Artifact closes the door explicitly instead of relying on nobody trying.

By contrast the Executor Accord Primitive (A.6.1.1.1.2.2.1) keeps a live In Progress Invocations Directory, because accords are ongoing operational instruments that get renewed and replaced.

The useful generalization: a governance framework needs to state which of its mechanisms are constitutive and therefore single-use, or a later actor can re-run a founding act and create ambiguity about which instance is authoritative.
description: Agent Creation, Prime Transformation, Executor Transformation and Agent Token all declare that no further Instances can ever be Invoked, and that no post-deployment process is needed.
